summary: Join our Humanitarian Law training course to learn vital skills for protecting civilians in conflict zones. Empower yourself to advocate for human rights.
lede: Humanitarian law and civilian protection training helps teams assess how operational choices affect civilian safety and reduce avoidable harm. Designed for program managers, protection officers, access and security staff, and sector teams, it covers interpreting humanitarian law, mapping threats and vulnerabilities, integrating safeguards into services, and communicating protection decisions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape or influence humanitarian operations, safety, access, and community outcomes.
audience: Humanitarian program managers and team leaders
Protection officers and coordinators (GBV, CP, HLP
Humanitarian affairs, civil-military coordination, and liaison officers
Government disaster response and refugee/asylum officials
Health, WASH, Shelter, Education, Food Security
Case management and community-based protection teams
modules: Foundations of Humanitarian Law in the Field
Understanding Protection of Civilians (PoC) in Practice
Access, Negotiation, and Engagement with Armed Actors
Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) and Community Trust
Designing a PoC Action Plan and Integrating it into Programs
Decision-Making Under Pressure and Protection Leadership
prerequisites: Participants should have a foundational understanding of humanitarian principles and prior experience in field operations. Familiarity with basic protection concepts is recommended but not required.
